passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
Your work location is the work region and country on your HR record, for example Colorado, US or Ontario, Canada. Your work location decides which rules apply when you work from somewhere else, whether that is business travel (§2) or temporary remote work (RSE-RW-01 §6).
For most employees the work location is the state or province of their home office. Remote-approved employees may have a different work region, which is recorded when their arrangement is approved. Keep your work location up to date: it affects payroll, benefits and which holiday calendar applies.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.section_heading: Business travel vs temporary remote work
passages.text:
Travel to do Ridgeline work at a client, a project site or a Ridgeline office is business travel, not temporary remote work. A business trip of up to 14 calendar days needs no Cross-Border Review, even when it is to another country. Longer stays, or working from another country for your own reasons, follow §3.
For example, a week at the Toronto office for project meetings is business travel for a Denver employee: the manager pre-approves it and no Cross-Border Review is needed. Spending several weeks working from a family home abroad is not business travel, even if you do your normal job while there.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
Contact HR before any permanent change of work location, to another state, province or country. A permanent move changes your HR record and may not be possible for every role.
A move can change your payroll, benefits, holiday calendar and Work Arrangement. HR will explain what changes and what needs to be approved. Moving before HR has agreed can leave Ridgeline unable to employ you in the new location.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.section_heading: Adding personal days to a trip
passages.text:
You may add personal days to a business trip. Personal days are taken as PTO under the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01), and the costs of the personal days are yours (RSE-EXP-01 §6).
Request the PTO in the usual way, with the usual notice and approval. Your holiday calendar is still your home office's calendar while you travel. Adding a few personal days doesn't turn a business trip into temporary remote work, provided you don't work on those days.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
Working from another country has extra security requirements, including notifying IT Security in advance; see RSE-SEC-01 §5.4.
HR approval and IT Security's checks are separate steps, and both are needed before you go. Use the VPN at all times while abroad.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.section_heading: Request at least 28 calendar days ahead
passages.text:
Request work from another country at least 28 calendar days before you plan to start, so HR has time to complete the review.
Requests made with less notice may still be reviewed, but HR may not be able to decide in time, and the request is more likely to be declined.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text: Working from another country, other than on a short business trip (§2.3), is always reviewed by HR, whatever the length. Your manager cannot approve it alone.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
You may work from another country for up to 20 working days per calendar year. Your manager cannot approve anything over the cap; HR reviews it as an exception, and it may not be approved.
Working days are counted on your home office calendar, excluding weekends and your company holidays. The cap counts all working days from another country in the calendar year, across every request. A stay of six weeks, for example, is around 30 working days and is over the cap.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
Open an HR ticket in the category remote_work, with your dates, the country and your work plan.
Your work plan should say what work you will do, how you will meet core hours across time zones and how you will keep project data secure. Tell your manager you have opened the ticket. HR's Cross-Border Review queue picks it up and may ask you for more detail.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
The Cross-Border Review is how HR checks a request to work from another country. HR looks at tax, immigration and work authorization, insurance, and payroll. Ridgeline does not give personal tax, immigration or legal advice; the review decides whether Ridgeline can support the request, and you may want your own adviser for personal questions.
The review protects both you and Ridgeline: working in another country can create obligations that neither side intended. HR may approve a request, approve it with conditions such as shorter dates, or decline it. HR does not tell you what you personally owe in tax or which visa you need.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
Temporary remote work within the state or province of your usual work location is allowed. Tell your manager where you'll be working.
No approval is needed, but you must still meet core hours and, if you are office-hybrid, plan around your anchor days. For example, an Austin employee spending a week working from family in another Texas city just tells their manager.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
Temporary remote work from another US state, or another province, needs your manager's approval for up to 30 calendar days per calendar year in total. Anything over 30 calendar days in a year needs HR review: your manager can't approve it alone, and HR decides.
The 30 calendar days count every day you are away, including weekends, and they add up across all trips in the calendar year. For example, a stay from the first of one month to the tenth of the following month is well over 30 calendar days, so it needs HR review even if your manager supports it. Submit the request in the HR Portal with your dates and location; HR reviews longer stays because working in another state or province can affect payroll and tax registration.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text: Temporary remote work means working for a period from somewhere other than your usual work location, such as a family home or a holiday rental, while doing your normal job. Travelling to do Ridgeline work at a client, a project site or another Ridgeline office is business travel, not temporary remote work; see RSE-LOC-01 §2.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
Field/site-based employees are not eligible for temporary remote work.
Their work depends on being at the project site. Travel to another site for work is business travel (RSE-LOC-01 §2).

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
Working from another country always needs HR review, whatever the length. See RSE-LOC-01 §3 for the rules and the Cross-Border Review.
Your manager can support the request, but cannot approve it. Plan well ahead: the review takes time, and there are notice and security requirements before you go.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
To change your Work Arrangement to remote-approved, submit a request in the HR Portal. Your manager endorses it and HR approves it; HR gives a decision within 10 working days. Remote-approved arrangements are reviewed annually and can be revoked if the role or circumstances change.
Explain in your request where you will work, how you will meet core hours and how you will stay connected with your team. If the request is declined, HR tells you why. You can ask again later, for example when your circumstances or role change.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
Field/site-based employees work at project sites. Their roles cannot be done remotely, so they are not eligible for remote-approved status or for temporary remote work.
Field/site-based employees may still do some office-based tasks, such as writing reports, at a Ridgeline office when their manager agrees. If a field/site-based employee moves into an office-based role, their Work Arrangement changes with the role.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text: Remote-approved employees work remotely most of the time. The arrangement must be approved by both the manager and HR. Remote-approved employees spend at least one week per quarter at their home office.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
To become remote-approved you need at least 6 months of service at Ridgeline and no active performance plan. Field/site-based roles and interns are not eligible. For contractors, remote work is set by their contract.
Meeting these requirements makes you eligible to ask; it doesn't guarantee approval. Your manager and HR also consider whether your role can be done well remotely, the needs of your projects and clients, and your team's ability to work together.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
This policy sets out where Ridgeline employees work: the three Work Arrangements, who can become remote-approved, how to request a change, the rules for working remotely, and temporary remote work away from your usual location. It applies to full-time, part-time and intern employees. Business travel is covered separately by RSE-LOC-01 §2.
Ridgeline believes engineering is best done with time together and time to focus. The arrangements in this policy aim to give teams regular in-person collaboration while allowing flexibility where the work allows it. Managers apply the policy fairly and consistently across their teams, and any questions go to the HR Service Desk.
